extracted.intended_audience: PhD students and postdocs preparing grant applications and planning academic/industry career transitions
extracted.subtask_description: Advice for PhD/postdocs on designing and sequencing fellowship, career-award, foundation, and SBIR/STTR applications to build a path to independence or industry. Emphasizes the three-document framework (research plan, career development plan, mentor statement) and alignment across documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants as career capital
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants are CV currency for academic and industry roles; even unfunded competitive proposals signal capability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Position grant-writing experience as demonstrable evidence of capability for faculty searches and industry roles (medical writing, grants administration, R&D management). Treat each application as a credential even if not funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence of postdoc awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursue an F32 (NRSA postdoc) before a K99/R00 transition award when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use earlier postdoc fellowships as stepping stones and practice for later career awards; plan timelines so applications build on each other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use foundation postdoc fellowships to bridge to faculty
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply to foundation postdoc fellowships (e.g., Burroughs Wellcome, HFSP, EMBO, Helen Hay Whitney) as a bridge to faculty positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target foundations that fund work similar to yours; multi-year awards from foundations can signal independence to search committees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reuse application infrastructure across submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each application is practice for the next; reuse and adapt previously developed materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refine and repurpose research plans, CVs, and training plans to save time and improve quality; expect a K99 to require 6–12 months to do well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-Document Framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant packages for career awards should include (1) Research Plan, (2) Career Development Plan, (3) Mentor/Sponsor Statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All three documents must align; reviewers look for consistency between the project goals, the training activities, and mentor commitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: The Research Plan explains what you'll do, why, and how.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the project clearly yours (not your mentor's), hypothesis-driven when appropriate, feasible within the award timeline, and framed as the start of your independent program; align aims with career development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career Development Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: The Career Development Plan details what skills you'll gain and the mentorship/training structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List specific named courses, workshops, and conferences; justify how each activity fills current skills gaps and supports transition to independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor / Sponsor Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentor statements document your team's commitment and qualifications to train you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentors should describe concrete training plans, quantify protected time and resources in letters of support, and demonstrate a track record of training successful independents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear trajectory to independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications should show a clear trajectory from current postdoc to independent investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the proposed work and training will evolve into an independent program and provide milestones that indicate progress toward independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor track record
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentors must have a track record of training successful independents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include examples of former trainees who achieved independence and explain how mentor experience will be leveraged for the applicant's development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressable skills gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal must identify skills the applicant currently lacks and show how the award will provide them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the mentor team explicitly covers those gaps and list concrete training activities or collaborations to gain those skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project that becomes your independent program
rubrics_metrics.description: The research project should be framed as the seed of the applicant's independent research program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid proposing a project that remains wholly embedded in the mentor's agenda; emphasize novelty and future directions that show independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Document institutional commitment (lab space, startup funds, protected time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters of support should quantify protected time, resources, and space; demonstrate how the institution will enable the applicant's transition to independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propose your own project (not mentor's)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not propose your mentor's project — propose YOUR project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear intellectual ownership of the idea, lead authorship on related work if possible, and explain how the project differentiates from mentor-led work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasible Specific Aims timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific Aims should be doable in the award period (example: 2 years for K99 + 3 years for R00 planned across five years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope aims to realistic milestones within the mechanism's duration and avoid over-ambitious or too-broad plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career Development Plan specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Career Development Plans must list specific named courses, workshops, and conferences rather than generic statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Naming concrete activities shows thoughtfulness and a realistic plan to obtain needed skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor team covers skill gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: The mentor team should explicitly cover the applicant's skills gaps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemble mentors whose expertise complements the applicant's deficits and document each mentor's role in the training plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters quantify resources and protected time
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters of support should quantify protected time and available resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong letters provide numbers/percent effort, commitments of space/equipment, and clear institutional promises rather than vague praise.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR Phase I expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase I focuses on feasibility, with typical budgets around $250–300K for 6–12 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate technical feasibility with preliminary data and a clear short-term plan; commercial viability should be addressed even in Phase I.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR Phase II expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase II focuses on full development with budgets around $1.5–2M over ~2 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a robust development plan, milestones tied to product development, and evidence of market and partner interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercialization plan importance in SBIR
rubrics_metrics.description: The commercialization plan comprises roughly half of an SBIR/STTR application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include market analysis, go-to-market strategy, revenue model, customer/partner letters, and milestones tied to go/no-go decisions; technical sections must address commercial viability as well as science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weight of letters of intent from partners
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters of intent from customers/partners are weighted heavily in SBIR/STTR review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secure concrete, signed LOIs that indicate real interest and potential commitments; vague expressions of interest are weak.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match project to foundation portfolio
rubrics_metrics.description: For foundation grants, match your project to the foundation's recent funded portfolio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the foundation's annual report and funded projects; target foundations whose priorities and recent awards align with your proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage foundation officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundation officers are accessible — call them before applying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use conversations to gauge fit, get feedback on proposal fit, and learn application priorities; this can improve your chance and avoid wasted effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smaller foundations tradeoffs
rubrics_metrics.description: Smaller foundations have less competition but smaller awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider applying to multiple smaller foundations for funding and visibility; balance award size with competitiveness and strategic fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-year foundation grants signal independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Receiving multi-year foundation funding can signal independence to search committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight multi-year awards on your CV and use them as evidence of an independent trajectory separate from mentor funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR industry rubric — commercial path and partners
rubrics_metrics.description: SBIR/STTR proposals must show a clear commercial path with named partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe customer segments, named partners/customers, partnership terms, and how partnerships advance commercialization milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR industry rubric — technical feasibility via preliminary data
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical feasibility must be demonstrated with preliminary data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide pilot results, prototypes, or proof-of-concept data that support feasibility claims and reduce perceived technical risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR industry rubric — market analysis (TAM/SAM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Market analysis must be realistic and include TAM/SAM estimations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show credible market sizing, addressable segments, and revenue assumptions; avoid overoptimistic projections without supporting evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR industry rubric — mixed team (business + technical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Teams should include both business and technical expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemble co-PIs or collaborators with commercialization, regulatory, or business development experience in addition to technical leads.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR industry rubric — milestones tied to go/no-go decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Milestones should be tied to clear go/no-go decision points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define objective criteria for milestone success and subsequent actions (pivot, scale, or stop) to show pragmatic project management.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR industry rubric — IP strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: An intellectual property strategy must be articulated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe patents, freedom-to-operate, licensing plans, or trade secrets and how IP will protect commercialization value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mismatched mechanism and career stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not apply to funding mechanisms that mismatch your career stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose mechanisms designed for your level (e.g., trainee awards for early postdocs) and explain why the chosen mechanism fits your trajectory; mismatch is a common reason for failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid projects that are too ambitious or too narrow
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects should not be unrealistically ambitious nor trivially narrow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance scope to be novel and impactful but feasible within the award timeline and resources; overly ambitious aims or tiny, incremental projects both weaken competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor team must cover proposed methods
rubrics_metrics.description: The mentor team must collectively cover all methods proposed in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If required methods are outside the mentor team's expertise, add collaborators or justify training that will supply the needed skills; reviewers penalize uncovered methodological gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid generic Career Development Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Generic training plans are weak; specificity is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide named activities, timelines, mentors responsible for each training element, and measurable skill outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims should be hypothesis-driven when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific Aims need a clear hypothesis-driven structure unless the mechanism allows exploratory work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State hypotheses and how each aim tests them, or explicitly justify a discovery/exploratory approach with appropriate evaluation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: K applications require clear path to independence
rubrics_metrics.description: K-series career development applications must show a clear path to independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail how the K support leads to independence (e.g., transition plan, protected time, milestones, and eventual R01-level readiness); lacking this is a top failure reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR partnerships must be concrete
rubrics_metrics.description: Industry partnerships in SBIR must be concrete rather than aspirational.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide signed letters, explicit collaboration terms, pilot customer commitments, or other tangible evidence of partnership to avoid reviewer skepticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Productivity aligned with career stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Productivity expectations should be proportionate to the applicant's career stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate an appropriate publication and productivity record for your stage; over- or under-claiming productivity relative to stage can hurt assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong external letters for trainee awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainee awards require strong letters from mentors and outside referees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secure letters that speak to training potential, prior accomplishments, and independent promise; outside referees should independently evaluate the applicant's readiness.
